title: VPC Connectivity
description: Explore public vs private subnets, bastion hosts, VPC peering, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, VPN, and Direct Connect.

data.text: Connecting Your VPC to the World

Once you have a VPC, you need ways to connect it to other networks. This might be another VPC, your corporate data center, or the internet. AWS provides several services for VPC connectivity, each designed for different scenarios.
Public and Private Subnets with Bastion Hosts

Public subnets have a route to an Internet Gateway and can be directly reached from the internet. Private subnets have no internet route. To manage private instances, you use a bastion host — a hardened EC2 instance in the public subnet that acts as a jump server.

data.title: Bastion Host Best Practices
items: Place the bastion host in a public subnet with a minimal security group allowing only SSH (port 22) from trusted IPs.
Keep the bastion host patched and monitored.
Use MFA for bastion host access.
Never store sensitive data on the bastion host.

data.text: VPC Peering, Transit Gateway, and PrivateLink

VPC Peering creates a direct network connection between two VPCs. Transit Gateway acts as a cloud router, simplifying connectivity between many VPCs and on-premises networks. PrivateLink provides private connectivity to services hosted by other AWS accounts without exposing traffic to the public internet.

rows: Simple, low-latency connection between two VPCs
Connect many VPCs and on-prem networks
Central hub-and-spoke model for large networks
No public IPs or internet routing needed
Connect VPC to corporate data center
Encrypted tunnel over the public internet
Consistent low latency and lower data costs

data.text: A Site-to-Site VPN creates an encrypted tunnel over the public internet between your VPC and your corporate network. AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated, private fiber connection from your premises to AWS. Direct Connect offers lower latency and more consistent performance than a VPN but requires physical infrastructure.

data.title: Create a VPC Peering Connection with AWS CLI
data.content: This example shows how to create a peering connection between two VPCs and accept it.
data.code:
# Create a VPC peering connection between VPC-A and VPC-B
aws ec2 create-vpc-peering-connection \
  --vpc-id vpc-aaaaaaaa \
  --peer-vpc-id vpc-bbbbbbbb \
  --region us-east-1

# Accept the peering connection
aws ec2 accept-vpc-peering-connection \
  --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-1234567890abcdef0

# Add a route to the route table of VPC-A
aws ec2 create-route \
  --route-table-id rtb-11111111 \
  --destination-cidr-block 10.1.0.0/16 \
  --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-1234567890abcdef0

terms.definition: A hardened EC2 instance used as a jump server to access private instances securely.
A direct network connection between two VPCs allowing private traffic routing.
A managed service that acts as a cloud router for connecting VPCs and on-premises networks.
A service that provides private access to services across VPCs without public internet exposure.
A dedicated private network connection from your premises to AWS.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Bastion hosts provide secure SSH access to private instances
VPC Peering connects two VPCs directly
Transit Gateway simplifies large-scale multi-VPC networking
PrivateLink enables private service access without public internet
VPN uses encrypted tunnels over the internet; Direct Connect uses a dedicated line
